newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coal tight ahead of negotiatons - BHP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coal tight ahead of negotiatons - BHP.

text.p: The hard coking coal export market remains in tight supply with the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd selling all the coal it can mine, Ian Dymock, manager public affairs for BHP Australia Coal, told Reuters on Thursday.
"We're loading ships as quickly as we can. (The buyers) probably can't get enough coal at the moment," he said.

Dymock was commenting on reports that Australia had opened skirmishing before this year's round of Australia-Japan coal pricing negotiations by asking for a US$6.00 a tonne price rise for hard coking coal.

Prices were not raised in formal meetings between Australian coal producers and Japanese buyers at the recent Australia-Japan business conferences in Sydney, Dymock said. "It seems to be after the meetings that (the $6.00 figure was raised)," he said.
The strengthening Australian dollar had been raised as a justification for a coal price rise but it was ultimately supply and demand which would make the difference, he said.
The supply/demand balance appeared similar to last year, with supply tight, he said.
Under changed parameters which emerged in the negotiating round for the current year, benchmark prices no longer apply, Dymock noted.
But average hard coking coal prices had emerged at about US$53.00 for the 1996/97 Japanese fiscal year, which ends March 31, he said.
Some very high quality hard coking coal prices had reached US$55.00/56.00 a tonne, while prices of lesser quality coking coal ranged down to US$48.00 a tonne, he said.
